propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, refugium nostrum et virtus: adesto piis Ecclesiae tuae precibus,
auctor ipse pietatis, et praesta: ut, quod fideliter petimus, efficaciter
consequamur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum
vivit et regnat in unitate.

refused.catholic-public-domain-version: Esth 14:12 is recorded as not carried by this edition: this edition prints Esther in the Septuagint arrangement and in fifteen chapters, so no Vulgate chapter or verse number addresses the matter it names: its 1:1 is the Vulgate's 11:2, its 3:1 is the Vulgate's 1:1, and its 13:9 is part of the king's letter and not Mardochai's prayer

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Da, misericors Deus: ut haec salutaris oblatio, et a propriis nos reatibus
indesinenter expediat, et ab omnibus tueatur adversis. Per Dominum nostrum
Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit.

provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 layer sets a semicolon after Sumpsimus where the 1962 sets a comma (see notes: this is likely scan damage, not the book); 1862 sets no comma after ut; 1862 sets a full stop before Qui vivis where the 1962 sets a colon; 1862 conclusion is the short cue Qui vivis et regnas. where the 1962 prints Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 40106-40111 prints the whole prayer: 'Sumpsimus Domine, sacri dona mysterii, humiliter deprecantes: ut, quae in tui commemorationem nos facere praecepisti, in nostrae proficiant infirmitatis auxilium. Qui viuis & regnas.' The 1570 prints it too at lines 81512-81518. Recorded limitation: ONE WORD INFERRED, NOT READ. The 1862 text layer damages infirmitatis at line 52486, which recognises as 'intinnitdtis'. I did not repair it silently: the word is supplied from the 1604 at line 40109 ('noftrae proficiant infirmitatis au- / xiiium'), which prints this prayer whole at the same place, and from the 1570 at line 81516. Confidence is medium for that reason. The semicolon at line 52481 ('SUmpsimus;') is very likely the comma-recognised-as-something-else damage the artifact record names, and the 1604 sets no mark at all there, but I record the layer as it reads rather than deciding for it. The 1862 reading rests on the text layer alone.

propers.text:

tui commemorationem nos facere praecepisti, in nostrae proficiant
